topic: The myth that eye contact always builds trust

script.title: Eye contact myth: why staring can hurt trust
script.hook: Does staring into someone's eyes ever backfire?

scenes.text: Does staring into someone's eyes ever backfire?

motion_action.headline: Does staring into someone's eyes ever

scenes.text: Eye contact can trigger threat responses in strangers.
Staring too long spikes the amygdala, raising anxiety.
Many people feel uneasy after a prolonged gaze.
A quick glance builds rapport; lingering looks signal dominance.
Cultural norms vary, but brief glances usually work best.
Some research suggests that looking away can lower perceived aggression.

motion_action.title: STUDY: GAZE AVERSION
motion_action.highlight_text: looking away can lower perceived aggression

scenes.text: Use brief eye contact, then look away naturally.
Overdo it and you’ll seem creepy, not confident.
Now you know the real rule:
